citation: Nunemaker et al. (2020). ORBIT: Offshore Renewables Balance-of-System and Installation Tool. National Renewable Energy Laboratory. https://doi.org/10.2172/1660132
description: ORBIT, the Offshore Renewables Balance-of-System and Installation Tool, estimates the activities, vessels, infrastructure and costs needed to construct offshore renewable-energy projects. U.S. national-laboratory contributors publish a Python package with documentation and technology-specific installation phases. Inputs are turbine and foundation design, site conditions, port and vessel assumptions and construction settings; outputs are project schedule and balance-of-system cost estimates. Geographic scope and study period are set by a project site and development scenario, not by a fixed national data layer. Apache-2.0 source is free from GitHub and PyPI. A limitation is that installation costs depend strongly on vessel rates, weather windows and supply assumptions; the package does not observe actual project spending. It can feed offshore wind capacity and infrastructure-investment simulations. The catalogue's data-ihdata-ihcantabria-wave-hindcasts is related environmental context that might inform site conditions after careful matching, but the link was not tested. No installation simulation was run.
inputs: Offshore project design, site, port and vessel parameters
